one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-12. (1) Q3 2026 results, expected around 10-12 November (date not yet confirmed by the company; Q2 came on 12 Aug) against guidance of $214-216M core revenue and a 38-40% core gross margin (8-K). The stock fell ~20% after Q1 on the margin guide (source 8), so the reaction distribution is wide; the Q4/FY2027 commentary (CFO: 'more than triple revenue in 2027') matters more than the print. (2) The main IPO lock-up ends two trading days after Q3 results or 180 days after the prospectus, whichever is earlier (~171M shares, about 5x the float sold; source 5), i.e. around 9-13 November. Field & Hanka find a -1.5% 3-day abnormal return at expiry, larger for VC-backed issuers (source 12); CoreWeave fell >9% in a day as insiders sold after its 2025 expiry (source 13). Against that, Schaeffer's broken-IPO study (stocks that closed >=25% above the IPO price then broke below it within six months, as CBRS did on 30 Sep) shows an average +7% one-month return with about half positive (source 9). Net: median slightly below spot (~$145.5, -2%) and a lognormal spread of ~27% for the month (below the inflated 115% realised/3.5 = 33%, above a no-event month), giving P(>=148.86) = 0.47.

fair_value.method: Blend of a 5-year DCF (WACC 14%, 13x FY2030 EBITDA exit) at $102.96 (40%) and 7x horizon NTM EV/sales on ~$4.07B at $128.82 (60%), with ~$4.6B net cash at the horizon and 257.3M diluted shares.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 18.7x (NVDA) to 107x (ARM), median 46.2x on the 8 peers with a forward figure; trailing EV/EBITDA 7.8x (SMCI) to 246x (ARM), median 63.8x; trailing EV/sales 0.57x (SMCI) to 50.7x (ARM), median 23.2x. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Cerebras has no meaningful earnings or EBITDA yet, so the multiple leg is EV/NTM sales: 7.0x at the horizon, in the lower third of the peer range and ~0.3x the peer median trailing EV/sales (forward peer multiples would be lower still for the hypergrowth names). Exit EV/EBITDA 13x on FY2030 sits between SMCI (7.8x) and NVDA (27.0x).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount, argued on structural differences that persist through the horizon: (1) gross margin ~41% core (FY2026 guide 41-43%, 8-K) vs 55-75% at the chip peers, because Cerebras sells capacity as a cloud and carries the data-centre cost; (2) customer concentration: MBZUAI 62% + G42 24% of FY2025 revenue and OpenAI a 'substantial portion' of projected revenue (424B4), with customers A/B/C at 76% of Q2 2026 revenue (10-Q); (3) capex at ~147% of revenue in H1 2026 means free cash flow is deeply negative through 2027. The closest economic peer, CoreWeave, trades 11.7x trailing sales on a ~103% forecast 3-year revenue CAGR, so 7x forward for Cerebras at ~50% NTM growth at the horizon is consistent with it. No sell-side 'outperform' call is used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$90 the equity is ~$23B, or EV ~$17-18B with about $5B of net cash left at the horizon: ~4x my FY2028 revenue, the CoreWeave-style distressed multiple. Trading there would most likely mean the backlog is impaired (OpenAI scaling back or re-sourcing the 750MW, or a cut to the $25.4B RPO) or that 2027 guidance comes in well under 'more than triple', rather than ordinary lock-up volatility.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine's reverse DCF says the 7x NTM EV/sales leg ($128.82) needs a 5.3% WACC to be matched by my explicit cash flows (FY2030 FCFF only ~$0.67B after 22% capex) plus a 13x exit. Put the other way: at a 14% cost of capital, 7x forward sales in late 2027 needs either long-run EBIT margins of ~30% (vs my 18% GAAP in FY2030) or growth of 20%+ well past 2030. Both are plausible only if Cerebras keeps a speed premium after the OpenAI MRA phases end. With the long-dated risks above (OpenAI re-sourcing 35%, GPU catch-up 40%) I treat 7x as a ceiling-ish base, which is why the DCF leg ($102.96) is below the multiple leg and I weight it 40%.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $49.8M (424B4); H1 2026 SBC $386.6M, of which $377.0M in Q2 on IPO-triggered vesting (10-Q, 8-K). The model uses GAAP EBIT (after SBC: ~55% of revenue in FY2026, 9% in FY2027 falling to 5%) and holds the share count flat apart from the OpenAI warrant, so SBC is counted once. Peers' trailing multiples are on a GAAP basis (secfacts); stockanalysis forward P/E is on a consensus (largely non-GAAP) basis, used only as context because the CBRS leg is EV/sales.

reasoning: Anchor: CBRS is a 5-month-old IPO that priced at $185 (~78x FY2025 sales of $510M), closed its first day +68% (source 8), peaked at $386 and has broken its offer price (now $148.86, -60% from peak). Base rates for this setup are poor on average but wide: Ritter's data show large IPOs lag the market by ~4% over three years (source 11) while 67.6% of broken IPOs have negative 3-year returns from the offer price (source 10); Schaeffer's broken-IPO study (>=25% above the offer, then below it within six months) finds a ~+8.9% average 1-year return, in line with the S&P 500, with only 37% beating it and a -13% median at six months (source 9). The closest analog, CoreWeave (2025 AI-cloud IPO, concentrated backlog), round-tripped from >$183 to ~$93 within three months of its lock-up and closed at about $77 on 2026-10-13 (secfacts peers run). Fundamentals: FY2026 core revenue guided $880-890M, CFO 'more than triple' in 2027, consensus $2.95B FY2027, RPO $25.4B, ~$7.0B net cash, but GAAP losses, ~147% capex/revenue and heavy customer concentration. My standard-model value is $118 (DCF $103 at 14% WACC with peer beta; 7x NTM sales $129), about 20% below spot. Ladder: rather than forecasting my fair value as the price, I blend it (~40%) with a market anchor at spot (~60%), because the sell side sits at a ~$292 average target (source 4) and the market is valuing a backlog I cannot fully underwrite. That gives a median near $130 and a mean near $148 (spot), with a right skew. Spread: three scenarios ($75/$140/$245; 33/47/20%) with ~32-40% within-scenario vol, roughly a 65-70% annual vol overall. That is below the 115% realised since listing (inflated by post-IPO price discovery) but above AI-hardware peers' ~60%. Tails: P(<$60) 10% (ample cash, ~$18/share at the horizon, limits a wipe-out), P(>$298) 6%. Macro: Kalshi's 2027 recession at 20% and a thin, stale Polymarket AI-bubble market at 21% (June) give no reason to shift the centre. Lane share: 11 of 28 sources are in lane; the 10 peer-statistics pages required by the 10-12 comps rule and three company filings make up most of the rest. Excluding those, 11 of 15 are in lane. Alpha Vantage consensus data matched StockAnalysis but is not cited because the feed needs a key; Twelve Data statistics were plan-locked.

defense_exposure.share_of_revenue: Not separately disclosed. Upper bound ~14% of FY2025 revenue and ~24% of Q2 2026 revenue; best estimate low single digits (judgment).
defense_exposure.detail: FY2025: MBZUAI (a UAE university) 62.0% and G42 (UAE AI company) 24.0% of revenue = 86%, both civilian (424B4). Q2 2026: customers A/B/C = 34%/32%/10%, B matching OpenAI's $56.8M (10-Q). Defense, military or intelligence customers could only sit in the residual 14% (FY2025) / 24% (Q2 2026), which also holds commercial customers (Cognition, Lovable, Block, Figma, AlphaSense, GSK, CrowdStrike per 8-K) and DOE national labs. The prospectus lists 'national laboratories, and defense organizations' only as possible on-premises customers and gives no revenue share. Neither filing reported a defense revenue line in the sections read.

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Peer median trailing EV/sales 23.2x (range 0.6x SMCI to 50.7x ARM; CRWV, the closest economic peer as an AI cloud with ~40%-type margins, 11.7x trailing). 7x NTM sits in the lower part of the range for structurally lower gross margin (core 41% vs chip peers 55-75%) and extreme customer concentration.

bull.story: OpenAI expands toward the 1.25GW option, AWS Bedrock launch lands in Q1 2027, FY2027 revenue beats $3.2B and the market pays 11x NTM sales.
